# InputService

[Framework](README.md) · `DotGame.Framework.Input` · class

```csharp
public sealed class InputService
```

Reads the keyboard and gamepads, and manages text input. Reach it as `Game.Input`. Pointers arrive as events on [`Game`](Game.md).

## Fields

### MaxGamepads

```csharp
public const int MaxGamepads = 8;
```

The gamepads the game can tell apart.

## Methods

### CreateTextInput

```csharp
public TextInput CreateTextInput()
```

Types: [`TextInput`](TextInput.md)

Creates a new text-input control backed by the platform's native editor. The control remains registered with the platform until [`TextInput.Dispose`](TextInput.md#dispose) is called. Subscribe to its events to observe edits, focus changes, submit, and cancel.

Use [`TextInput.Bounds`](TextInput.md#bounds) to position the editor's transparent overlay over the on-canvas text field. Call [`TextInput.Focus`](TextInput.md#focus) from a tap-gesture handler to give keyboard focus synchronously inside the trusted gesture (this is required by iOS Safari to bring up the soft keyboard).

### GetGamepadState

```csharp
public GamepadState GetGamepadState(int index)
```

Types: [`GamepadState`](GamepadState.md)

Returns a gamepad as it is this frame, for polling during the update phase. One that isn't connected reads as nothing held. No allocation is performed.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `index` | Which gamepad, from 0 to one less than [`MaxGamepads`](#maxgamepads). |

### GetKeyboardState

```csharp
public KeyboardState GetKeyboardState()
```

Types: [`KeyboardState`](KeyboardState.md)

Returns the keyboard as it is this frame, for polling during the update phase (e.g. continuous movement). No allocation is performed.
